candidates.title: Antigonish, N.S., sign condemned for depicting rape culture
candidates.description: A sign hung outside an off-campus house in Antigonish, N.S., during St. Francis Xavier University's homecoming weekend is being described as an example of rape culture and has drawn condemnation from two universities and a professor who teaches at St. FX.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'This is not reconciliation,' judge says, scolding Canada for dragging feet on First Nations land debt deal
candidates.description: A federal judge recently said the way Canada has continued to "shirk its responsibilities" to a group of Manitoba First Nations since signing a landmark agreement meant to resolve historic treaty land shortages "is simply not acceptable."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Toronto Sixers rally past Vancouver Warriors to repeat as Canada Super60 women's cricket champions
candidates.description: The Toronto Sixers successfully defended their Canada Super60 Cricket League women's title Saturday night at B.C. Place in Vancouver, beating the previously undefeated Vancouver Warriors by six wickets with three balls to spare.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: A swordfish was found on Haida Gwaii. Will more follow?
candidates.description: A University of British Columbia researcher says the finding is unusual but no longer unexpected due to warming waters worldwide, including in Canada.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Juno-winning singer Sass Jordan dead at 63
candidates.description: A post on Jordan's social media page on Saturday says she died the day before "surrounded by her loving family." It called her an "inimitable force of nature" and "irreplaceable being of light and joy."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: String of Grindr assaults in North Vancouver prompts safety warning from Pride group
candidates.description: North Vancouver RCMP are investigating a series of assaults involving victims they say were targeted through the Grindr dating app.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman, 2 children dead after serious collision near Foam Lake, Sask.
candidates.description: A serious car crash left three people dead and four others injured. A 40-year old man from South Carolina was arrested and charged.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Montreal Canadiens defenceman Lyle Odelein, who won a Stanley Cup in 1993, dead at 58
candidates.description: Montreal Canadiens defenceman Lyle Odelein, who won a Stanley Cup with the team in 1993, has died at the age of 58. The Canadiens confirmed Odelein's death in a statement Saturday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 3 Cape Bretoners were hit and killed by a train in Maine in 1970. Some want the case reopened
candidates.description: Kenny Novak, 15, David Burrows, 17, and Terry Burt, 20, were in sleeping bags on a rail track west of the border town of Houlton, Maine, when they were struck early on the morning of July 10, 1970, by a train. The deaths were ruled accidental, but questions persist about the deaths.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: B.C. lawyer found to have misappropriated $117K from dementia-stricken client
candidates.description: Leonard Hil Marriott also prepared documents to give himself 50 per cent ownership of the woman's condo and 75 per cent of her estate.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Internal documents detail Ottawa's economic worries over Alberta referendum
candidates.description: Internal federal documents offer insights into how Ottawa is assessing the economic fallout from the possibility of Alberta separating from Canada and becoming an independent state.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada bet billions on an EV boom. Was it too much, too soon?
candidates.description: The federal and provincial governments bet billions on the rapid rise of the electric vehicle industry. But major EV and battery projects in Ontario, Quebec and British Columbia have since been delayed, cancelled, suspended, substantially changed — and in one case, gone bankrupt — as automakers and suppliers adjust to weaker-than-anticipated demand.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Actor and advocate Michael J. Fox promoted to companion level in Order of Canada
candidates.description: Celebrated actor and Parkinson's disease activist Michael J. Fox said he felt both "pride" and "humility" while receiving a promotion within the Order of Canada on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What does Elections Alberta's compliance agreement with Forever Canadian mean?
candidates.description: A compliance agreement between Elections Alberta and a group campaigning for Alberta to remain in Canada means the organization is required to disclose certain referendum advertising expenses and contributions.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Judge in fatal N.L. case questions whether impaired driving sentences are working
candidates.description: A St. John's judge is questioning whether or not punishments are fitting the crime when it comes to impaired driving. Judge Bruce Short sentenced a man to five years in prison on Friday for a fatal crash in 2023.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After Trump’s Venezuelan oil deal, those living on polluted lake in oil country wait for change
candidates.description: In late August, the U.S. signed a sweeping oil deal with Venezuela's interim authorities to control a share of the country's oil. In one of the largest oil-producing regions, residents welcome promises to revitalize the industry, they also have a more immediate demand: clean up the polluted lake.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cornell president calls alleged gang rape 'deeply disturbing,' pledges greater transparency
candidates.description: Scrutiny has mounted in recent days over Cornell's response to allegations that the woman was sexually assaulted by multiple fraternity members in 2024. The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, has sued the university and seven former students.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The King will never live at Buckingham Palace. What does that mean for the monarchy?
candidates.description: While there have been efforts to emphasize that Buckingham Palace will continue to be the working and ceremonial headquarters of the monarchy, the recent confirmation that King Charles won’t be living there could also be sending signals about the institution and its future.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Russia to intensify strikes on Ukraine after Zelenskyy remarks, defence ministry says
candidates.description: Russia will intensify strikes on targets in Kyiv and other regions of Ukraine following recent remarks by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the Russian Defence Ministry said on Sunday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pro-Ukraine governing coalition wins 35% in Latvian election
candidates.description: Latvian lawmakers on Sunday planned to begin negotiations to form a new government following a parliamentary election in which pro-Ukraine prime minister Andris Kulbergs's four-party coalition emerged with 35 per cent of the vote.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Mark Carney for Nobel Peace Prize? Probably not, but his name's out there
candidates.description: If relations between Canada the U.S. are cool now, the temperature could plummet if Prime Minister Mark Carney were to win the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize this year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canada scores a dairy win on U.S. soil as farmers grumble about Trump's trade war
candidates.description: At the World Dairy Expo in Wisconsin, the political tension between Canada and the U.S. is — more or less — set aside as farmers from both sides of the border focus on their best bovines. But even so, CBC News found some Americans in the crowd who take a dim view of the Trump administration's trade war.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli strikes kill 5, including 4 women, in Gaza, health officials say
candidates.description: An Israeli airstrike killed at least five Palestinians, including four women, in an apartment building in Gaza City early on Saturday, health and civil defence service officials said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Christa Pike on ventilator after surviving Tennessee execution attempt, lawyer says
candidates.description: Christa Pike, convicted of killing a classmate in 1995 when she was 18, is receiving breathing assistance from a ventilator after Tennessee's attempt to execute her by lethal injection failed earlier this week, her attorneys say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ottawa launches new national AI council to advise on safety, deployment
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney's new national council on artificial intelligence is meant to provide the government with guidance on the evolution of its AI strategy and on making the technology safer.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Undetected software issue knocked out 911 for several provinces last month, Bell report says
candidates.description: A 911 outage that lasted nearly an hour and a half in several Canadian provinces last month was caused by a previously undetected bug in Bell's software, the company said in a report on Friday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Carney, Smith say new West Coast pipeline could get oil companies building again
candidates.description: It's been a relatively quiet decade in Alberta's oilsands, but the federal and provincial governments believe a new West Coast pipeline coupled with policy shifts might help turn up the volume. Prime Minister Mark Carney and Alberta Premier Danielle Smith say that if oilsands companies start building again — as they hope — it will be different this time around.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
candidates.description: Footage shows a drone hitting the Pivnichyi (Northern) Bridge as vehicles move across it, creating a large fireball.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: What we know about Russian strikes on Kyiv bridges
candidates.description: BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson is near Kyiv's Northern Bridge, which has been hit for the second day in a row.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Indian police accused of sexual harassment against journalists at protest
candidates.description: The allegations were made after police detained dozens of protesters demanding the resignation of the election chief over changes to voter rolls.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Australia investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
candidates.description: State police and the country's security agency are looking into the co-pilot, who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: What to know about Brazil's election pitting Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro
candidates.description: Polls suggest the election will be a closely run contest between the left-wing incumbent and his right-wing rival.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: 'Anger in the streets': Tens of thousands protest in Spain over housing crisis
candidates.description: More than 50 protests took place on Saturday after the government failed to get emergency legislation through parliament.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
candidates.description: Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations of a woman who says she was drugged and gang raped as "deeply disturbing".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US father and son arrested after 'gas station heroin' deaths
candidates.description: They are accused of selling at least one student derivatives of kratom, often called "gas station heroin" in the US.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why Canada is wargaming a (long shot) US invasion
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the military is running scenarios in the unlikely case the US invades Canada.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?
candidates.description: For the first time in three decades there has not been a single Atlantic hurricane in September, normally the most active month.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why has Brazil accused the US of election interference?
candidates.description: The Latin American country will vote for its next president, as Lula da Silva and Bolsonaro clash over sovereignty, security and ties with Washington.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Will Spain's housing crisis lead to a snap election?
candidates.description: The BBC's Guy Hedgecoe is in Madrid, where a series of marches have been scheduled, after Spain's Congress rejected measures aimed at tackling the country's housing crisis.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Newly released video shows Luigi Mangione’s arrest
candidates.description: The bodycam footage also shows a police officer finding a gun in Mangione's backpack, days after the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How widely used is the death penalty in the US?
candidates.description: The death penalty is back in the news after Christa Pike survived two lethal injection attempts in Tennessee - but how widely used is it in the US?
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: I'm a wildlife cameraman but 'special' rare sightings can still take me by surprise
candidates.description: Wildlife cameraman Dan Abbot is caught off guard by a humpback whale, a rare sight in Welsh waters.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Hawaii's iconic 550-year-old Hōlei Sea Arch collapses
candidates.description: The lava rock formation protruding from the rocky cliffs of Volcanoes National Park crumbled some time last weekend.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Woodlands project records more trees than expected
candidates.description: The Lost Woods of the Low Weald and Downs project aims to restore some of Sussex's ancient woodland.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: U.S. Marine arrested for alleged murder of a woman in Okinawa, Japan
candidates.description: Japanese police arrested a U.S. Marine in the alleged robbery and murder of a woman on Okinawa, officials said Sunday.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: She died covering war for Fox News. Her parents blame the network — and a star reporter
candidates.description: The family members of two Fox News journalists killed while covering the war in Ukraine are suing the network, saying it put getting the story ahead of its people.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: For some Brazilians, this election is a vote on Trump
candidates.description: President Trump says he's been having success winning races in Latin America. As Brazilian voters go to the polls, they're also deciding how much influence Trump should have in their country.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: France arrests 5,000 people, mostly teens, as school protests spread
candidates.description: High school students say their classrooms are overcrowded, teachers are missing and buildings need repairs. The protests have spread to cities across France, and some 5,000 people have been arrested.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. withdrawal from Iraq is complete
candidates.description: Twenty-three years after President George W. Bush's campaign of "shock and awe," the U.S. military has completed its withdrawal from Iraq.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Lula or Bolsonaro? Some Brazilian voters say they don't want either
candidates.description: Brazil's election enters its final day of campaigning as Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro make their last pitches to voters. Brazilians explain what worries them, and why some still can't choose.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Brazil's big political rematch: What to know about the Brazilian election
candidates.description: Four years after President Lula narrowly defeated Jair Bolsonaro, Brazil is back at the ballot box. This time, Lula faces Bolsonaro's son, Flávio, in a high-stakes rematch.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How Brazil's two leading presidential candidates are talking about crime
candidates.description: Crime is at the top of voters' concerns in Brazil ahead of Sunday's national elections. Many are calling for tougher measures — part of a broader rightward shift across Latin America.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: The G7 will release 100 million reserve barrels of diesel fuel over the next 4 months
candidates.description: After increased pressure from Washington, the G7 held an emergency meeting on energy. The world's wealthiest nations say they will release 100 million barrels of oil and diesel fuel in their reserves.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: G7 countries reluctantly agree to tap their fuel reserves to help the U.S.
candidates.description: G7 nations plan to release large amounts of diesel fuel soon, but European countries were not entirely happy about the agreement.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Economist Betsey Stevenson breaks down the gender gap in recent hiring reports
candidates.description: The U.S. economy added fewer jobs than expected last month and unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. NPR's Scott Simon talks to Betsey Stevenson, an economist at the University of Michigan.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: 4 ways to battle performance anxiety, according to a confidence coach
candidates.description: Worried about stumbling before a high-stakes event, like a race or a job interview? Psychologist Cindra Kamphoff offers creative strategies to overcome the jitters and build confidence in the moment.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 4 at 3:41PM AST until October 4 at 3:45PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
candidates.description: The heavy rain has ended. However, ponding of water over roads remains possible due to previous rains. Please continue to heed remaining road closures.

candidates.description: * WHAT...Significant waves to 6 ft occasionally to 8 ft expected. * WHERE...Burns Harbor to Michigan City IN. * WHEN...From 1 AM to 10 AM CDT Monday. * IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

candidates.description: * WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures near 110 degrees and overnight lows only getting down to around 85 degrees. This will yield at least major heat risk, impacting anyone without adequate cooling and hydration. * WHERE...Elevations in Death Valley National Park below 2000 feet. * WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday. * IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during extreme heat events.

Dauphin Island.

candidates.description: At 329 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm capable of producing a landspout near Bunnell, moving east at 15 mph. candidates.description: SMWLIX The National Weather Service in New Orleans has issued a * Special Marine Warning for... Coastal waters from Pascagoula Mississippi to Stake Island out 20 NM... Mississippi Sound... * Until 315 PM CDT. * At 222 PM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing waterspouts was located 17 nm south of Horn Island, moving northeast at 15 knots. HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater. SOURCE...Radar. IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage vessels and oil rigs...and create suddenly higher waves.
